questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intervals on Which a Radical Function Is Continuous
questions.problem: Determine the largest interval on which the function $f(x)=\sqrt{6+x}+\sqrt{5x+10}$ is continuous.
questions.worked_solution:
Our function consists of two radical functions, so it is continuous over all points in its domain.

- To find the domain of $\sqrt{6+x}$, we set the expression under the radical to be greater than or equal to zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}6+x\ge 0\,⟹\,x\ge -6\end{aligned}
$$

- To find the domain of $\sqrt{5x+10}$, we set the expression under the radical to be greater than or equal to zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+10\ge 0\,⟹\,5x\ge -10\,⟹\,x\ge -2\end{aligned}
$$

The domain of $f(x)$ is given by the intersection of the domain of our radical functions:

$$
[-6,\infty )\cap [-2,\infty )=[-2,\infty ),
$$

and the function is continuous on this interval.

- To find the domain of $\sqrt{12-4x}$, we set the expression under the radical to be greater than or equal to zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}12-4x\ge 0\,⟹\,4x\le 12\,⟹\,x\le 3\end{aligned}
$$

- To find the domain of $\sqrt{5x+8}$, we set the expression under the radical to be greater than or equal to zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+8\ge 0\,⟹\,5x\ge -8\,⟹\,x\ge -\frac{8}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

The domain of $f(x)$ is given by the intersection of the domain of our radical functions:

$$
(-\infty ,3]\cap [-\frac{8}{5},\infty )=[-\frac{8}{5},3],
$$

and the function is continuous on this interval.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intervals on Which a Rational Function Is Continuous
questions.problem: Determine the largest union of intervals on which the function $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}-x-2}{x-2}$ is continuous.
questions.worked_solution:
This is a rational function, so it is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we start by factoring the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{2}-x-2}{x-2} \\  & =\frac{(x+1)(x-2)}{x-2} \\  & =x+1,\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $x\ne 2.$

This function is continuous everywhere except at the excluded point $x=2.$

Therefore, the domain consists of the union of the intervals $(-\infty ,2)$ and $(2,\infty ),$ namely

$$
(-\infty ,2)\cup (2,\infty )
$$

and the function is also continuous on this union of intervals.

$$

questions.problem: The interval $I$ consists of all real numbers $x$ such that $-2\pi \le x\le 0.$ What is the largest subset of $I$ on which the function $f(x)=\operatorname{cot}⁡(x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)$ is continuous?
questions.worked_solution:
Trigonometric functions are continuous at all points in their respective domains.

The function $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is continuous over the entire interval $[-2\pi ,0],$ but the function $\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ is not defined at $x=-2\pi ,-\pi ,0.$ 

Therefore, the domain of $f(x)$ consists of the union of the intervals $(-2\pi ,-\pi )$ and $(-\pi ,0),$ namely

$$
(-2\pi ,-\pi )\cup (-\pi ,0)
$$

and the function is also continuous on this union of intervals.

questions.problem: Find the largest union of intervals on which the function $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3}{{x}^{2}-1})$ is continuous.

The function is a composition of two functions, a rational function, and a sine function.

The sine is continuous at all points in its domain, and its domain consists of all real numbers. So, we focus on the rational function.

Likewise, the rational function $\frac{3}{{x}^{2}-1}$ is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we start by factoring the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{3}{{x}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{3}{(x-1)(x+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

This function is continuous everywhere except at the excluded points $x=-1$ and $x=1.$

Therefore, the domain our original function consists of the union of the intervals $(-\infty ,-1),$ $(-1,1),$ and $(1,\infty ),$ namely

$$
(-\infty ,-1)\cup (-1,1)\cup (1,\infty )
$$

and the function is also continuous on these intervals.

canonical_examples.problem: Determine the largest union of intervals on which the function $f(x)=\dfrac{x-3}{x^2-5x+6}$ is continuous.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
This is a rational function, so it is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we start by factoring the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x-3}{{x}^{2}-5x+6} \\  & =\frac{x-3}{(x-2)(x-3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2},\end{aligned}
$$

where $x \neq 3$.

This function is continuous everywhere except at the excluded points $x=2$ and $x=3.$

Therefore, the domain consists of the union of the intervals $(-\infty, 2),$ $(2,3),$ and $(3, \infty),$ namely

$$
(-\infty, 2)\cup(2,3)\cup(3, \infty)
$$

and the function is continuous on these intervals.
